SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Watery diarrhea × 3 days, 5–6 loose stools/day; began after two episodes of vomiting (vomiting now resolved).
- Associated symptoms: Feels dehydrated, weak, decreased appetite; felt mildly febrile on day 1, afebrile now. Denies abdominal pain, hematochezia, headache, myalgia.
- Past medical history: Asthma.
- Medications: Salbutamol (blue) inhaler, dose/route/frequency not documented; no other regular medications.
- Social history: Lives alone; software engineer; non-smoker; infrequent social alcohol use.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Family history: Father—hypertension, deceased from bowel cancer; Mother—type 2 diabetes.

Objective:
- No in-person examination performed (telehealth visit); no vitals provided.
- No investigations performed or reviewed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhea
   - Assessment: Likely acute viral gastroenteritis.
   - Investigations planned: None at present; consider stool studies or in-person assessment if symptoms persist > 1 week or worsen.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) as directed.  
     • Encourage liberal clear fluids.  
     • Paracetamol as needed for fever or malaise (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
     • Rest and remain off work until diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours (anticipate another 1–2 days off).  
   - Follow-up: Return visit or seek care sooner if no improvement by next week, inability to tolerate fluids, bloody stools, high fever, or worsening symptoms.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: Vital signs, abdominal exam, complete medication list (including dose/frequency of inhaler), immunization status.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; no inaudible sections.
